newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.200 to 1.000 cent per higher while pork bellies were called 0.250 to 0.100 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Carryover demand from sharply higher to limit up close and further strength in cash markets were expected to boost hog futures at the start. Cash hog prices continue to rise, pork cutout values are strong and there is continued expectations of an international draw on U.S. pork products due to the Taiwan pork ban, analysts said.
Hog futures posted new contract highs in all months Thursday and the trend is seen continuting, they said.

However, some analysts are starting to belive the market may be near a top, especially after a large spike up in the volume on Thursday. The new lean contracts set a record volume and this can sometimes indicate a top or a bottom is near, they said.

Further demand is also seen in pork bellies after limit gains in nearby months Thursday. Further demand is seen following the strong tone to cash bellies, light pace of slaughter and recent word that Japan is in the market for U.S. pork bellies. Cash bellies are up to best levels since early October and hog kills are running four percent under projections from the last Hogs and Pigs report, they said.
However, evening up and profit taking could develop ahead of the monthly USDA Cold Storage report Friday aftrernoon. High cash prices will also shut off domestic demand for bacon, they said.
Analysts' expectations on the amount of bellies in cold storage April 1 in the USDA report ranged from 49 to 53.2 million lbs versus 47.655 million on hand last year.

But the report may have little impact since movement of product into storage since April 1 has been running well below year ago. Stocks could easily fall back below year ago levels during April, they added.
